generatedProse.concept-context: In any subject, exams are built to support your learning, not only to measure it. A short test checks that core ideas are secure, while a longer written exam asks you to weigh evidence and argue a case. Both deepen your understanding as you prepare, and both give your tutor a fair, shared view of how everyone is doing.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students who have just received the same module result, which included an exam.

Student A sees the exam as a hurdle now behind them. They reread their notes the night before, sat the exam, and have not thought about it since. For Student A, the exam was something to survive, and its only meaning is the mark.

Student B treats the exam as part of learning. While preparing, they noticed which ideas they could not yet explain and went back to them, so revision taught them something. Sitting the exam to time also showed them they can build an answer under pressure. For Student B, the mark is real, but so is what the exam built.

Both sat the same exam. Only Student B saw it as a learning tool, and took from it more than a grade.
generatedProse.summary: An exam is a learning tool, not just a hurdle. It supports your development, gives your tutor a level view of how everyone is doing, and builds skills such as working to time under pressure. You can now explain what exams are for and recognise someone who treats one as something to learn from. The next lesson looks at the forms these exams take.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Student B do that showed they saw the exam as a learning tool?

items.text: They used revision to find and fix gaps in their understanding, and valued the skills the exam built.
They reread their notes the night before.
They forgot about the exam as soon as it was over.
They cared only about the mark at the end.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using revision to learn, and valuing the skills built, is seeing the exam as a learning tool.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Student B did beyond chasing the mark.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Student B treated the exam as a learning tool: revision found and fixed gaps, and the exam built skill under pressure. The other options only survive or chase the mark.
